text:
morgan: heads up — ran into a confusing bug in the Python SDK streaming helper in our onboarding sample app. Users calling it from an async FastAPI handler get TypeErrors or the handler blocks. Repro below.

alex: can you paste the callsite?

morgan: minimal usage from sample-app (async handler):
```py
@app.get('/events')
async def events():
    async for chunk in client.events_stream({})
        yield chunk
```
The SDK currently ships events_stream typed as Iterator[bytes] in the stub, and the runtime returns a sync iterator wrapped in an async generator helper — it's a mess. On CPython the above sometimes blocks the event loop (sync iterator used inside async context) and mypy complains.

jun: Oof. That explains the reports from onboarding where users paste our snippet and see "'async for' requires an object with __aiter__". Are we sure the stub is wrong or the runtime implementation?

morgan: both. Runtime returns a small wrapper object that implements __iter__ and __aiter__ but with subtle behavior: __aiter__ returns self and __anext__ is defined as a normal function that calls .__next__ via run_in_executor for compatibility. If loop is special (uvloop vs asyncio) we see blocking or double-wrapping. Also our SDK does an internal retry on 401 refresh that replaces the underlying socket and creates a fresh iterator — but we don't close the previous iterator cleanly, so background threads can linger.

tasha: yikes. Two problems: type stubs wrong (Iterator vs AsyncIterator) and lifecycle mismatch on retry. Priority-wise which we fix first?

alex: typing fix is quick: change stubs to AsyncIterator[bytes] / AsyncIterator[str] depending on mode, and add overloads for sync vs async usage. But we also need a runtime guard: if the caller is in an async context and we detected a sync-only iterator, we should raise a clear error with remediation.

jun: proposal: introduce a new API object StreamingClient.stream_context() that returns an async context manager exposing an AsyncIterator. Internally it will wrap any sync iterator safely (offload to threadpool + ensure aclose()/close() is called on finish) and also attach a finalizer that attempts to close underlying transport on GC. Add a docs note showing correct FastAPI usage: "return StreamingResponse(client.stream_context(...))" vs naive async for.

tasha: for retries we can implement a "handoff" pattern: when a token refresh occurs, mark the old iterator as drained and schedule aclose() on it, but continue yielding from the new iterator. Also add a diagnostic metric for leaked iterators.

morgan: I've got a failing unit test in the sample-app that reproduces both symptoms (mypy error + leaked thread). I'll open a PR with a type change + runtime wrapper and a small integration test that runs under both asyncio + uvloop.

alex: extra ask for docs: add a short FAQ "Why does my async handler block when streaming?" that explains sync vs async iterators, the recommended helper, and an example conversion helper to use in user code if they already have a legacy sync iterator.

dev-bot: Issue created: SDK-1159 (py-stream-typing-sync-async-confusion) — assigned to devex and eng-runtime.

jun: follow-up: add mypy CI job to sample-apps that runs the examples with strict typing. It will catch broken stubs early.

morgan: thanks all — PR incoming with tests + docs link. I'll ping here once merged. :rocket:
